newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - August 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - August 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Speculation by financial markets of another Reserve Bank official interest rate cut, fuelled by poor retail sales in June, saw bond rates fall to a 25-year low yesterday. Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showed the seasonally-adjusted value of retal trade fell 1.8 percent last month, with monthly sales volumes below the level of last August. Page 1.

Foster's Brewing Group chief executive Ted Kunkel is expected to ask Canada's Molson Group of Companies for an explanation of their plan to take over Foster's joint venture Molson Breweries. Kunkel said Foster's 40 percent stake in Molson was a core asset and would not be sold. Page 37.

BT Funds Management has decided to establish a separate division which will offer administrative services to other funds managers. BT head Ian Martin said the new division would offer services including record keeping for investors, and settling and accouting for all funds managers' transactions. Martin said BT could be a formidable competitor in the sector. Page 37.

ANZ Investment Bank and Bank of America have organised Crown Ltd's refinancing of A$650 million in existing bank loans and organised further credit and working capital. A company spokesman said the banking syndicate had aggressively pursued Crown, resulting in better terms for the company, which is keen to expand into Asia and buy the management rights of the Crown complex. Page 38.

James Hardie Industries Ltd chairman Alan McGregor told the company's annual meeting yesterday that expanding overseas operations and revenue meant shareholders would probably see a large reduction in the level of franking credits on dividends, and the end of the dividend reinvestment plan this year. Page 39.

Stockfeed and salt group Ridley Corporation Ltd yesterday filed a prospectus in each Canadian province for the A$65 million sale of nearly half its stake in Canadian subsidiary Ridley Canada Ltd by public float. The Canadian company will be listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, with Ridley retaining a 58 per cent stake. Page 39
THE AUSTRALIAN

The 1997 Corruption Perception Index by Transparency International has ranked Australia as the eighth least corrupt nation in a survey of 52, awarding a 8.86 score out of a possible 10. The ranking is an improvement for Australia, with Transparency International praising the Federal Government's plans to use the tax system to expose bribes paid to foreign officials. Page 21.

Office equipment business Ausdoc has recorded an annual net profit of A$19.44 million due to improved sales last September. Ausdoc managing director Peter Reilly has forecast further growth this year from both new and core businesses, saying the company was on the lookout for strategic acquisitions should the opportunity arise. Page 23.

The market continues to be cautious concerning troubled grocery wholesaler Davids, slashing almost 21 percent off its market capitalisation over two days. The loss of confidence follows the management shake-up in which John David resigned as executive chairman and chief executive and the announcement of an abnormal loss of A$262 million for the half year. Page 25.

Australia was the world's largest market for privatisation in the first half of 1997 with the privatisation of the Victorian power industry being a significant contribution. The trend is set to continue with the upcoming Telstra float and the planned privatisation of the New South Wales electricity industry. Page 23.

The Australian Industrial Relations commission yesterday approved a A$100 million retrenchment program proposed by telecommunications company Telstra. The company still has further labour obstacles to overcome with negotiations beginning for a new enterpise bargaining agreement covering Telstra's entire workforce of 65,000. Page 21.

The devastating landslide at Australian ski resort Thredbo, which has trapped around 20 people, is not expected to have long-term negative consequences for entertainment and hospitality company Amalgamated Holdings (AHD). The Thredbo ski resorts were part of Amalgamated Rydges Hotel's division, which accounts for only a third of AHD total revenue. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday an El Nino drought, predicted by the Bureau of Meteorology, put at risk the 3.75 percent economic growth estimate. He added that the Budget forecast of two percent annual average employment growth could not be met, though the through-the-year forecast of 2.25 per cent by mid-1998 would be. Page 29.

Consumers have continued to shift their spending toward discount stores, leaving the department stores hardest hit by the fall in retail sales. In June, retail sales fell by 1.8 percent, with department store sales falling by 10.5 percent, and spending has been higher in food and homewares sales. Page 29.

Queensland-based Northern Building Society and First Provincial Building Society yesterday announced the merger of their two companies and indicated they were considering extra partners in New South Wales. The new body, First Australian Building Society, will have total assets of A$1.1 billion and be the fourth largest building society in Australia. Page 31.

General Property Trust admitted yesterday sluggish retail growth was making it difficult for the shopping centre company to achieve profit growth in its annual pay-out to its 74,000 unitholders. The company yesterday announced a 62.8 percent increase in net income to A$110.9 million but this only translates into a small rise in distributions to 10.4 cents or a rise of 0.3 cents. Page 31.

Junior gold company Bendigo Mining NL's plans to build a mine at Bendigo were scuttled yesterday after leading shareholder Kerry Packer withdrew from a planned capital raising. Bendigo Mining announced Packer's company Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd had chosen not to exercise its rights in the A$34 million raising, and therefore would not underwrite the issue. Page 33.

Well-known investment bank and broker Merrill Lynch Australia is considering applying for a banking licence as part of its long-term plan to become a combined banking and broking service for high-value customers. Merrill Lynch Australia joint chief execuive John Magowan and a delegation from the company's international private client division met with the Reserve Bank of Australia to discuss the issue. Page 31.
THE AGE

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday warned that Australia's unemployment forecast of 8.25 percent would not be met, and that economic growth might have to be reduced. His comments followed the release of figures yesterday showing a 1.8 percent fall in retail sales in June and earlier figures of a 4.5 per cent fall in housing approvals. Page B1.

The Federal Government urged banks to pass on in full the Reserve Bank's 0.5 percent cut in official interest rates. The Commonwealth and ANZ Banks reduced their home loan rates by a smaller figure, leading Treasurer Peter Costello to urge customers to shop around, as Small Business Minister Peter Reith said businesses should demand the full cut be passed on. Page B1.

Weak retail sales in June have hit department stores the hardest as consumers continue to shift their spending toward discount stores. Department store sales fell 10.5 percent, while the overall value of retail sales fell 1.8 percent for June, the fifth fall in the past ten months. Page B1.

News Ltd-backed Pacific Sports Entertainment yesterday sold its 60 percent stake in the Brisbane Bandits baseball club to minority stakeholder and original owners Braxbury Pty Ltd. PSE's plan to create a franchise operation covering several sports has ben undermined by problems with its main drawcard, the Brisbane Broncos Super League team. Page B1.

The Council of Textile and Fashion Industries of Australia has accused the Industry Commission of giving misleading figures on consumer benefits from the scaling back of tariffs for the TCF industries. The Council says gains for consumers would only equa about A$64 million a year, and disputed the Commission's claims that tariffs costs consumers A$19 billion annually. Page B3.

Crown Casino has finalised a refinancing of A$650 million of bank-debt facilities clearing the way for future capital raising to finance new ventures and purchases. The refinancing agreement is a major step forward for the company, as it previously operated under project-debt regulations which restricted its activities and gave it limited control over its bank debt. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
